title: A Mars Orbiter Photographs an Interstellar Comet
hook: China's Tianwen-1 turned its camera on 3I/ATLAS as the interstellar comet swept past Mars — catching its tail and coma from another planet's orbit.
key_points: 3I/ATLAS is a comet from beyond our solar system, passing through on a one-way trip.
China's Tianwen-1 Mars orbiter imaged it as the comet raced past Mars.
The faint images show the comet's tail and its glowing coma.
Observing from Mars orbit gave a vantage point no Earth-based telescope could match.
The material shedding off it was born around another star.
content_html: Interstellar comets are rare and fleeting: they fall in from the dark, whip past the Sun once, and leave forever. So when 3I/ATLAS came through, observers used whatever they had — including a spacecraft parked at another planet. China's Tianwen-1 Mars orbiter captured a faint but remarkable view of the comet as it raced past Mars, according to a ScienceDaily report, resolving both its tail and its glowing coma.
extra_html: The appeal isn't the picture's sharpness — the target was dim and far from the camera's design job of mapping Mars. It's the material. Everything streaming off 3I/ATLAS condensed around some other star, which makes each observation a free sample of chemistry from another planetary system. And observing from Mars orbit offers a geometry no Earth-based telescope can reproduce: a different angle on the same coma, at a moment that will never repeat.

related.title: Methane on an Interstellar Comet
related.hook: A comet from another star system swept through ours — and the Webb telescope caught methane on it, the first time that molecule has been seen on a visitor from beyond.

related.title: A Wobbling, Peanut-Shaped Asteroid Reshaped by Sunlight
related.hook: NASA's Lucy found that asteroid Donaldjohanson is a peanut-shaped relic of an ancient collision — slowly reshaped by sunlight, and still carrying traces of old water.

related.title: A tiny universe in a bottle reveals clues to the origins of life
related.hook: Researchers grew real cosmic dust from scratch in a glass tube, recreating space's harsh conditions to study how life's raw ingredients might form and hitch a ride on comets.

choices.text: It formed outside our solar system, so its material comes from another star
It is the largest comet ever recorded
It orbits Mars rather than the Sun

flashcards.explanation_html: 3I/ATLAS is an interstellar comet — a visitor passing through. The gas and dust it sheds are samples of material born beyond our solar system.

flashcards.back_html: The glowing cloud of gas and dust surrounding the nucleus, released as solar heat vaporizes its ices. Tianwen-1's images captured both the coma and the tail.
